items.heading: These Are Narrower Than
items.text: These are narrower than a platform checklist and narrower than the general online-delivery questions, because a counselling session is a narrower thing than either, one bounded conversation meant to resolve one decision.

items.heading: "Counselling" Gets Stretched to Cover
items.text: "Counselling" gets stretched to cover a lot of different formats. These are the specific things worth telling apart before you book, and what to check for each.

items.heading: These Three Questions Sound Similar
items.text: These three questions sound similar but aren't the same comparison, and mixing them up leads to reading the wrong page or booking the wrong product.

items.heading: The Single Biggest Check
items.text: The single biggest check is fit: a counsellor can be broadly qualified and still be the wrong match for your exact decision type.

items.heading: A Real Counselling Session Ends
items.text: A real counselling session ends in a recommendation. If it stays open-ended, it has quietly become a guidance conversation instead, whatever it was booked as.

items.heading: Online Delivery Adds One More
items.text: Online delivery adds one more layer worth checking, the sensitive detail you share for one sitting deserves the same care online as it would across a table.
